name: Avid Pro Tools
note: Every keyboard row of Avid's "Pro Tools Shortcuts Guide", version 2025.6 (created 5/20/2025). The guide prints an Action column and separate Mac and Windows columns, and both are carried over as written; the context is the guide's own section heading (Playback, Recording, Edit Modes and Edit Tools, Edit Selection, Definition, and Navigation, Editing, Nudging, and Trimming, MIDI Note Editing, Zoom, Automation, Fades, the menu sections, the Workspace and Browser sections, and so on), falling back to the chapter title where a chapter has no sections. Avid writes Command, Option, Control and Start; these become Cmd, Alt, Ctrl and Win, so a Windows chord such as "Control+Start+P" is Ctrl+Win+P here. Where a row gives one set of modifiers with two keys ("Command+ ] or [") or two whole chords ("Shift+Up Arrow/Shift+Down Arrow", "Left/Right Arrow keys", "Page Up/Down") it is split into one action per key and the key is appended to the name in parentheses. Where a row lists genuine alternatives ("Option-click on Zoomer tool or Option+F") the first alternative this grammar can express is kept. A few rows only give a shortcut for one of the two platforms; those carry only that platform. Left out because the grammar cannot express them: every mouse row (clicks, double-clicks, drag and drop, modifier-clicks on Transport buttons, faders and Zoomer tool), every numeric-keypad row (the whole Transport Mode (Numeric Keypad), Shuttle Mode (Numeric Keypad) and Step Input sections (Avid states the Step Input window shortcuts need the Enable Numeric Keypad Shortcuts option), the numpad Nudge and Plus/Minus rows, and every row Avid marks "(on numeric keypad)"), the rows whose shortcut is a held modifier or a described gesture, and the rows in the Keyboard Shortcuts window chapter that are printed as prose rather than in the Action/Mac/Windows tables.
